figures.finding: The NZFC invests up to NZ$2.5 million of equity (or a grant up to NZ$500,000) in a feature with significant New Zealand content by an experienced NZ producer; New Zealand government money together may not exceed 90% of the financing (unless the NZFC puts in NZ$500,000 or less), and a grant applies where the NZFC puts in NZ$500,000 or less on a budget of NZ$1 million or less.
figures.applies: New Zealand, NZFC Feature Film Production Investment (Terms of Trade effective 22 December 2025, page read 2026-11-01).

sources.said: Equity investment of up to $2.5 million … Grants of up to $500,000 … The applicant must be an experienced New Zealand producer

A NZFC Investment of NZD$500,000 or less AND where the film’s budget is NZD$1,000,000 or less will be a grant. … must not exceed 90% of the total financing for the film. … the equity investment is no more than $1,500,000 and your film is being funded due to Innovation being the main stated ambition; or … the equity investment is no more than $500,000. … with a budget over NZD$1 million.

figures.finding: New Zealand productions get a 40% cash rebate on qualifying NZ spending, capped at NZ$12 million per production (40% of NZ$30 million); a theatrical feature must spend at least NZ$1 million from 1 July 2026 (NZ$2.5 million before) and raise at least 10% of its budget from non-NZ-government sources; international productions get 20%, plus 5% for those passing a points test.
figures.applies: New Zealand Screen Production Rebate (administered by the NZFC for the Ministry for Culture and Heritage), criteria effective 1 July 2026.

sources.said: The New Zealand Rebate is 40% of QNZPE. The New Zealand Rebate is capped at $12 million per production. … (Maximum Rebate = $12 million)

of Qualifying New Zealand Production Expenditure (QNZPE) up to NZ$30 million … Feature Film (theatrical release) … NZ$1 million … from 1 July 2026 … The expenditure threshold for feature films that started principal photography before 1 July 2026 is NZ$2.5 million. … Feature films: At least 10% of budget from non-NZ government sources. … You, or your production company, need to demonstrate at least 18 months active engagement in the New Zealand screen industry.
New Zealand's 20% and 5% Uplift cash rebates … NZ$4 million

figures.finding: The rebate does not count business overheads above 5% of qualifying NZ spending or NZ$400,000, whichever is less, and caps financing fees (executive producer fees included) at 2% of the finance; the NZFC sets no fee percentage, asking that overheads and above-the-line fees be relative to the budget and consistent with industry norms, and gives the producer 50% of any underspend and, on films without the rebate, a 50% corridor and 50% of net profit.
figures.applies: New Zealand, NZSPR criteria effective 1 July 2026; NZFC Terms of Trade (22 December 2025) and Feature Film Production Investment FAQs (July 2026).

sources.said: Costs generally considered by the NZFC to be “business overheads” above 5% of the QNZPE or $400,000 whichever is the lesser … financing fees (such as loan or arrangement fees and executive producer fees) are capped at 2% of the amount of the finance.

Production company overheads and above-the-line fees (e.g. script development, writers, directors, producers, and key cast) should be: … relative to the film’s budget; … consistent with industry norms; and

It is a general requirement that any underspend of the film’s budget is allocated 50% to the producer … For films that are not accessing the NZSPR, we will give the producer a 50% corridor of our recoupment position. … • 50% to the producer; and

figures.finding: Spada represents New Zealand's independent screen producers; members pay a levy of 0.1% of the total NZ production budget on the first day of principal photography.

sources.said: Spada is proud to represent Aotearoa New Zealand's leading screen producers and production companies. … The levy is a flat rate of 0.1% of the total NZ production budget, regardless of format or genre, and is payable on the first day of principal photography.

figures.finding: In 2024/25 the NZFC funded 12 new feature films and gave finishing grants to seven; its funded features drew 668,160 admissions in New Zealand cinemas (251,386 the year before), two of them over 50,000; sales of NZFC films brought in NZ$3.47 million, of which NZ$1.60 million went back to the NZFC, which recovers at most its own investment in each film.
figures.applies: New Zealand, NZFC financial year 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025; applications received are not given.
